## Introduction

This is a simple demo to carry out variable selection 

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```

```{r setup}
library(fspls2)

##set the types
  options("fspls.types"= jsonlite::fromJSON('{"gaussian":["correlation","rms"],"binomial":["AUC"],"multinomial":["AUC"],"ordinal" : "AUC_all"}'))

  ## set the y_transforms to explore  
  transform_y=getYTransform(pow = 1,  n_random=1, perm=F)
  ## set the flags
  flags = list(min=0,  #minimum number of variables
               max=200, # maximum number of variables,  
               nfold=10,## number of folds.  10 fold implies a 10 non-overlapping 10% splits
               batchsize=0, ##batchsize can be specified alternatively to nfold, but only one can be nonzero
               angles_only=F, ## whether to use purely angles to find best variables
               topn=50,  ## if using model fit to rank variables, how many top angles to take  (larger takes more time)
               beam=1, ## how many best combinations to take through to next round of iteration. minimum value is 1, but higher explores more combinations
               all_v_all=F,  ## for multi-class outcomes, this builds all vs all classifier, instead of a one vs all
               project=T,   ## whether to use the projection approach in model building (TRUE recommended)
            useglmnet=T,  ##whether to useglmnet for model fitting (after variables selected) (TRUE recommoneded)
                        verbose=F,
            mc.cores=2,  ## only works in unix
            direction="none" ## can be + , - or none
    )

```

```{r example}
  examples = c("binomial", "gaussian", "ordinal", "multinomial");
  example="gaussian"
  
  #FUNCTION TO SHOW HOW TO RUN EACH EXAMPLE
  runExample<-function(example){
    fi = system.file("extdata", paste0(example,"_data.rds"), package = "fspls2")
    dataset = readRDS(fi)
    dh = dataH$new(dataset$dataset, y = dataset$y, nme=example, flags=flags, transform_y = transform_y, dbDir=NULL)
    analysis =analysisEnv$new(flags=flags, dbDir=NULL) ;
    #analysis$clear_db(drop=T, datasH = list(dh))
    datasH = list(dh)   
  #  system.time({
#this is the step that has parallelisation over folds
    vars_all = analysis$select(datasH,  flags, transform_y, phens = dh$pheno()$all)
  #  })
    all_models =dh$makeAllModels(vars_all,useDB=F)
    eval1= dh$evaluateAllModels(all_models, useDB=F)
    ggps1=plotEval2(eval1,legend=T, grid1=c("subpheno","pheno","cv_full"), grid0="measure",linetype="data", ##"full_model"
                   shape_color=c("data","transf"),sep_by=c("beam"), showranges=T,
                   scales="free",title =names(phens)[1], title1="pheno" ) #, grid="pheno~cv_full",showranges = F)
  
    return(ggps1[[1]])
  }
```
Example 1
```{r example1}
  runExample(examples[1])
```
Example 2
```{r example2}
  runExample(examples[2])
```
Example 3
```{r example3}
  runExample(examples[3])
```
Example 4
```{r example4}
  runExample(examples[4])
```
